newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-SHAQUILLE O'NEAL TO MISS 8-10 WEEKS WITH KNEE INJURY.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-SHAQUILLE O'NEAL TO MISS 8-10 WEEKS WITH KNEE INJURY.

text.p: Los Angeles Lakers All-Star centre Shaquille O'Neal will be out eight to 10 weeks because of ligament damage in his injured left knee, the team announced.
A magnetic resonance imaging test Thursday revealed a hyperextended knee with damage including a torn capsule, a fractured bone and a partial tear of the lateral co-lateral ligament.
Surgery is not required, but O'Neal will wear a splint for two to three weeks before beginning what is expected to be a long rehabilitation process.
O'Neal, who missed two games and the All-Star Game last week with an ailing right knee, injured his left knee in the first quarter of Wednesday's 100-84 victory over Minnesota.
He suffered the latest injury when he became tangled with Minnesota's Dean Garrett trying to grab an alley-oop pass.
O'Neal stayed in the game for another five minutes and scored the Lakers' next 10 points before leaving with 3:37 left in the quarter. He did not return and finished with 12 points and four rebounds.
O'Neal accompanied the Lakers to Denver, where they were to play the Nuggets Thursday night.
In O'Neal's absence Wednesday, forward Elden Campbell moved into the pivot and had 21 points, nine rebounds and four blocks.

The 7-foot-2 (2.18 metres), 320-pound (145 kg) O'Neal suffered the right knee strain on February 4 against the Washington Bullets. Team doctors diagnosed the injury as a strained medial collateral ligament and O'Neal sat out a loss to the Los Angeles Clippers and a win over the Chicago Bulls before the All-Star break.
Voted earlier this season as one of the league's 50 greatest players of all time in just his fifth season, O'Neal was not in Cleveland over the weekend for All-Star festivities.
He was one of five All-Stars to sit out the game with an injury, but the other four attended the mid-season affair.

O'Neal left the Orlando Magic to sign a seven-year, $123 million deal with the Lakers in the off-season. He is averaging 25.9 points, 12.9 rebounds and three blocks in 46 games. The Lakers owned the best record in the West at 36-13 heading into Thursday night's game.
